svg.aria-label: Diagram: what an AWS Organizations tag policy evaluates and what it does not. AWS states that in a tag policy you specify tagging rules applicable to resources when they are tagged, and that untagged resources or tags that are not defined in the tag policy are not evaluated for compliance with the tag policy. A resource tagged with an allowed value is compliant; one tagged with a disallowed value is non-compliant and its tagging request is refused where enforcement is on for that resource type; a resource tagged with different capitalisation is treated as carrying a different key, because capitalization treats CostCenter, costCenter and Costcenter as unique tag keys; a tag not named in the policy is not evaluated; and a resource with no tags at all is not evaluated either. Enforcement prevents noncompliant tagging requests from completing and can prevent resource creation where tag values do not meet requirements, but basic compliance rules do not enforce tag compliance on resources created without tags and cannot ensure that required or mandatory tag keys are configured at resource creation. AWS directs customers to use SCPs to prevent IAM users and roles from creating certain resource types if the request does not include the specified tags. Enforcement applies only to supported resource types, and where a service propagates tags to resources it creates, enabling enforcement may block dynamic scaling and provisioning.
svg.title: A tag policy is a schema for tags that exist
svg.text: The resource with no tags is not non-compliant. It is out of scope.
“you specify tagging rules applicable to resources when they are tagged”
WHAT A TAG POLICY SEES
CostCenter=Finance allowed value compliant
CostCenter=Finnance wrong value non-compliant; refused if enforced
costcenter=Finance different key “unique tag keys” under capitalization
Owner=jay not in the policy NOT EVALUATED
(no tags at all) NOT EVALUATED
Which is why a tag policy compliance report is not a tagging coverage report.
Enforcement constrains values, not presence — AWS states its own limit
“Basic compliance rules do not enforce tag compliance on resources that are created without tags.
This capability does not enforce missing tag keys. You cannot use this capability to ensure that required or
mandatory tag keys are configured at resource creation.”
What is refused is a tagging request that does not match the schema.
And it names the control that does make tagging mandatory
“Use SCPs to prevent IAM users and roles in target accounts from creating certain resource types if the
request doesn’t include the specified tags.”
Two policies, two jobs
SCP: the keys that must be present at creation.
Tag policy: the values and case those keys use.
Most estates need both and install one.
Before enabling enforcement
Where a service propagates tags to resources it
creates, enforcement “may block dynamic scaling
and provisioning”. Check the child, not the parent.
The audit: compare the compliance report against a plain resource inventory.
The difference between them is the untagged estate, and the first document cannot see it by design. Close
together means your problem really was consistency. Far apart means a tag policy was never the answer.
Compliance is read in AWS Resource Groups; the policy lives in Organizations.
